title: Q-CTRL Achieves RTCA DO-160 Airworthiness Qualification for Ironstone Opal Quantum Navigation - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Quantum infrastructure and sensing company Q-CTRL has announced that its Ironstone Opal quantum magnetic navigation system has achieved safety-of-flight qualification under the commercial aviation RTCA DO-160 environmental testing standard. Unveiled ahead of live demonstrations at the Farnborough International Airshow, the milestone marks the first quantum navigation payload certified for commercial aerospace and uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) deployment.

Rising global incidents of GPS jamming and spoofing—disrupting more than 1,500 commercial flights daily—have prompted aviation regulators and defense agencies to seek passive alternatives to satellite-based positioning. Unlike conventional inertial navigation systems that accumulate positional drift over long flights, Ironstone Opal measures subtle variations in Earth’s crustal magnetic field using atomic quantum sensors and matches them to onboard geomagnetic maps.

To operate reliably inside magnetically noisy aircraft frames, the platform pairs quantum magnetometers with AI-driven software ruggedization that filters out airframe interference in real time. The passive, non-emitting architecture has undergone flight evaluations with commercial and defense partners, including Airbus and Lockheed Martin, as well as U.S. defense programs.

Details on the DO-160 qualification are available from Q-CTRL here, alongside background on Q-CTRL’s flight trials with Airbus here and Lockheed Martin’s quantum PNT overview here. Related QCR coverage of Q-CTRL’s $24.4M DARPA Robust Quantum Sensors (RoQS) award is available here.
